newsitem.title: USA: Retaliate if no US-EU meat pact in week - US senator.
newsitem.headline: Retaliate if no US-EU meat pact in week - US senator.

text.p: The United States should retaliate against European meat exports if there is no agreement in a week on the nettlesome "veterinary equivalency" issue, U.S. Sen. Charles Grassley said Monday.

"If no agreement can be reached by April 1, I urge you to consider strong retaliatory measures against the European Union's exports of meat to the United States," Grassley, R-Iowa, said in a letter to U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky.
The two sides have disagreed for years over meat inspection procedures.

If there is no action by April 1, Grassley said he would press for passage of a bill that would allow unilateral U.S. action or prompting a demand for a World Trade Organization ruling on the dispute.
U.S. and EU officials were expected to meet on the matter this week.
U.S. Agriculture Department has warned the EU that it might bar shipments of meat unless they came from plants that "specifically adhere to and meet U.S. regulatory requirements."
